Main charitable entity types: Federal registered charity (CRA), incorporated charity (Canada Not-for-Profit Corporations Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: No citizenship requirement for trustees, but a Canadian address must be maintained for records and filings (a registered agent suffices).
Est. cost & time: C$300 (C$100–200 incorporation + C$100 charity registration); incorporation 2–4 weeks, charity registration 35 days–3 months
Notes: English/French; no foreign-formation ban; popular with diaspora and dual-citizen charities; ongoing CRA reporting obligations are substantial.

Main charitable entity types: State nonprofit corporation (e.g., Delaware, California), private charitable trust, 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
Key local requirements: Registered agent and state address in the state of incorporation; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Est. cost & time: US$100–500 state filing + US$400–600 IRS Form 1023 fee; incorporation days–2 weeks, 501(c)(3) determination 6–12 months
Notes: The most common foreign-founder pathway: state nonprofit corporation + 501(c)(3); fully remote; no charity regulator, only tax-exempt status.

Main charitable entity types: None — no private charitable sector; state-affiliated solidarity funds only
Key local requirements: No charitable registration is open to foreign nationals; all civil-society bodies must be state-sanctioned.
Notes: Foreign formation is effectively barred; use a Canada/US entity and partner with a local state-linked body instead.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee, charitable trust (deed), nonprofit corporation
Key local requirements: Jamaican registered office and local company secretary/agent; no citizenship requirement for directors; English.
Notes: No formal charity status, regulator, or donation tax-deductibility regime; most foreign founders use a company limited by guarantee + local manager.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2019), charitable trust, nonprofit society
Key local requirements: Bahamas registered office and licensed registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Strong offshore-agent ecosystem; no income tax so no tax-exempt registration is needed; donations are not tax-deductible for donors.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2016), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + agent; no citizenship requirement for directors; English.
Notes: No dedicated charity regulator; standard expat path is a company limited by guarantee with a local secretary.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2019), charitable trust, society
Key local requirements: T&T registered office + local agent; no resident-director requirement; English.
Notes: Gifts to approved charitable organizations are income-tax deductible (T&T Income Tax Act); no formal charity status beyond government approval.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Established offshore-agent services make remote formation straightforward; no charity tax regime.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Agent services in English; little charity-specific legislation; company limited by guarantee is the standard vehicle.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Strong offshore-agent infrastructure; remote formation in English is practical.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2015), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Agent services available; no charity regulator; English-language filings.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Agent services in English; minimal charity-specific legislation; company limited by guarantee is the standard form.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Key local requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Notes: Offshore-agent ecosystem; English; no formal charity status.

Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (fundación, Law 479-08), association (asociación)
Key local requirements: Notarial deed (acta notarial) — in person or via apostilled special power — local seat and local fiscal; Spanish-language documents.
Notes: Spanish bureaucracy; the notarial deed (in person or certified power of attorney) is the main hurdle; Chamber of Commerce registration and RNC tax ID required.

Main charitable entity types: Declared association (association déclarée, Law No. 30 of 1943), NGO branch/representative office
Key local requirements: Founding deed before a Haitian notary, physical seat in Haiti, local legal representative/director; French.
Notes: French-language notarial deed plus registration with the public prosecutor; a local partner is effectively required; high security/political risk.

Main charitable entity types: asociación civil (AC); fundación (Civil Code); fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: 3+ founders, notarized Spanish-language articles, Mexican legal address; no citizenship requirement, then SAT RFC registration.
Notes: Donataria autorizada (DA) status with SAT is a separate multi-month step required for tax-deductible donations; English-speaking notary/lawyer services readily available in Mexico City.

Main charitable entity types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación; fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, Guatemalan legal address, Registro de Comercio filing; foreign founders permitted.
Notes: No dedicated charity registry or donor tax-benefit regime; notary and registry processes are slow; everything in Spanish.

Main charitable entity types: non-profit company (limited by guarantee); registered charity (Charities Act 2020); trust
Key local requirements: 2+ directors (foreigners OK, no residency requirement), local registered office and company secretary via local agent; documents in English.
Notes: English-speaking, simple Companies Registry; most expats form the non-profit company first and add charity registration later; local service providers handle everything.

Main charitable entity types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación (Ley 2011); fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: Spanish-language articles, local address, registry filing under the 2011 Associations and Foundations Law; foreign founders permitted.
Notes: Donor tax benefits are limited; NGOs receiving international funds should also register in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs NGO directory.

Main charitable entity types: fundación; asociación; ONGD (registered development NGO)
Key local requirements: Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Personas Morales plus Registro de ONGD (Chancillería) filing for NGOs.
Notes: International ONGDs must register in the Registro Público de ONGD; moderate bureaucracy; all filings in Spanish.

Main charitable entity types: asociación; fundación (Ley de Fundaciones); fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: Spanish articles, local address, Registro Nacional filing; formally open to foreign founders.
Notes: Avoid: government has dissolved 5,700+ NGO legal personalities since 2018, including foreign-funded ones; laws target foreign-financed civil society, so an Australian-founded charity faces extreme cancellation/political risk.

Main charitable entity types: asociación o fundación sin fines de lucro (single law); fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Comercio; 3+ members for an asociación, single founder for a fundación.
Notes: Stable, professional services widely available in English; donor tax exemption requires separate Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) approval.

Main charitable entity types: fundación de interés privado (FIP); asociación; fideicomiso (trust)
Key local requirements: Spanish articles and name, local registered office, board of 3+ members, IFPF registration; single foreign founder permitted, no local nationals required.
Notes: The FIP (Ley No. 8 de 2000) is the most popular expat foundation vehicle in Latin America; IFPF is a specialized fast registry; strong English-language support.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (incorporated association), Corporación (2016 hybrid)
Key local requirements: No nationality requirement for board; Colombian registered address, Colombian lawyer to execute the public deed and register with the Cámara de Comercio; filings in Spanish.
Notes: Most expat-friendly in the region; foreigners can be president/directors; Bogotá has strong English-speaking legal market; donation tax deductions require separate DIAN certification; 2023 NGO-law reforms (Ley 2287/2022) added transparency reporting for foreign-funded entities.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (incorporated association), Corporación (corporation)
Key local requirements: Local (Venezuelan) resident officers and registered office, Venezuelan lawyer, notarized deed; severe currency controls (CADIVI/SICR) on bank accounts and foreign donations.
Notes: Major political/economic risk; 2010 Ley de ONGs lets the state restrict entities; foreign funding heavily scrutinized; most international NGOs operate through foreign legal entities, not Venezuelan ones.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación civil (incorporated association), Institución de utilidad pública (IUP, public-benefit institution)
Key local requirements: Minimum 3 founders; Ecuadorian resident president/board and local address; Ecuadorian lawyer; 2023 reform (Ley 2023-13 / COEP regime) added registration and foreign-funding reporting obligations.
Notes: Foreign founders permitted as members/board; Spanish-language documents; IUP status adds time and a public-benefit declaration; banking and tax (SRI) onboarding is slow.

Main charitable entity types: Asociación civil (civil association), Fundación (private foundation), Instituto (non-profit institute)
Key local requirements: Public deed registered with SUNARP; local registered office; president/legal rep should be resident in Peru for banking; filings in Spanish.
Notes: No nationality requirement; foreign founders allowed; tax exemption (exoneración) from SUNAT is separate, discretionary and needs annual reporting; Lima is the practical hub; English not official.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (social organization), Cooperativa (cooperative)
Key local requirements: Resident (Bolivian) officers, local address, notarized deed; 2023 NGO law (Ley 1417, replacing 1993 Ley 1475) requires registration and restricts foreign funding, advocacy and political activity of foreign-funded entities; Spanish only.
Notes: Foreign NGOs must register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería); 2023 law caps foreign government funding for certain activities and tightens oversight; heavy Spanish-language bureaucracy; few English speakers.

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit company (NPC, 2018 Act), Friendly society (Friendly Societies Act), Co-operative society
Key local requirements: Guyanese registered office and resident directors; English is official; no citizenship requirement for board but a local presence is needed; no restrictions on foreign donations.
Notes: Easiest bureaucracy in the sub-region and English-speaking; non-profits face extra scrutiny at formation and take longer than companies; tax exemption is discretionary (Commissioner of Inland Revenue); friendly societies are the most common non-profit form.

Main charitable entity types: Stichting (Dutch-style private foundation), Vereniging (association)
Key local requirements: Surinamese notary (deeds in Dutch), local board/office in practice; 2013 Dutch-style Civil Code permits stichting with foreign elements but a local notary and presence are required in practice; Dutch language barrier.
Notes: Dutch is the working language — the main barrier; small legal market; banking requires a local presence; few English-speaking professionals; new Civil Code (in force 2013) modernized foundation law but practice is conservative.

Main charitable entity types: Associação (association), Fundação (private foundation), OSC/OSCIP (social organization, Law 9.093/1995)
Key local requirements: Minimum 2 members (association) or 1 founder (foundation); Brazilian CNPJ and local address; notarial deed registered with a cartório; foreign founder may join the board; filings in Portuguese.
Notes: Heavy red tape (famous bureaucracy); main hurdles are getting a CPF and a bank account (foreign-inflow/câmbio rules); OSCIP certification gives donation tax deductions; 'instituição de utilidade pública' (federal/municipal) is a long, discretionary extra step.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación civil (civil association), Cooperativa (cooperative)
Key local requirements: Local registered office and a local representative; notarized deed; founder may be foreign; registration with the relevant ministry/civil registry; Spanish documents.
Notes: Under-regulated and relatively tolerant of foreign founders, but the legal market is small and Spanish-only; tax exemption requires separate certification; fewer English-speaking lawyers than neighboring countries; slower administration than Chile/Argentina.

Main charitable entity types: Asociación (association), Fundación (private foundation, public or private interest)
Key local requirements: Minimum 3 persons (association); local registered office; foundation requires a local representative; registration with the Registro Nacional de Personas Jurídicas; Spanish filings.
Notes: Very stable, low political risk; foundations enjoy tax incentives (50% exemption on qualifying income); English reasonably available in Montevideo business circles; 'declaración de utilidad pública' optional.

Main charitable entity types: Asociación civil (civil association, Ley 23.851), Fundación (private foundation, Ley 27.290/2016), Cooperativa (cooperative)
Key local requirements: Local registered office and resident director/legal rep; foreign founder/trustees allowed; notarial deed registered with the commercial registry (personas jurídicas); Spanish filings.
Notes: Most expat-friendly bureaucracy in South America; English widely spoken in Buenos Aires; foreign founders can serve on boards; donation tax exemption is a separate AFIP step ('Ingreso a Régimen de Entidades Exentas', Ley 24.976); 2016 foundation law made fundaciones cheaper and faster than the old regime.

Main charitable entity types: Asociación (association), Corporación (corporation), Fundación de derecho privado (private foundation, Ley 20.839/2015)
Key local requirements: Chilean registered office; board may include foreigners; legal representative should be resident in Chile; public deed registered with the Conservador de Bienes Raíces; Spanish filings.
Notes: Fast, clean bureaucracy; the de facto hub for LATAM expats and many run foundations/associations there; English widely used in Santiago legal market; donor tax deduction requires 'calificación' from the tax authority; 2015 law modernized foundations.

Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (хувийн сан); Association (нийгмийн эвлэл); NGO under the 2013 NGO law
Key local requirements: As a Mongolian citizen you register with the Legal Entity Registration Office (LERO, Justice ministry) with a Mongolian-language notarized charter, a local registered address, and a governing board (minimum 5 members for non-membership NGOs); a foundation requires an endowment adequate to its stated purpose.
Est. cost & time: Modest state fees (tens of USD) plus notarization; typically 2–8 weeks for registration.
Notes: Scored on the local-citizen route, which is straightforward — no foreign-founder bar. The pure foreign-founder route is much harder: a foreigner must usually form a foreign-invested legal entity (LLC, ~$100,000 minimum investment per investor) and rely on a local agent, with in-person Mongolian-language steps and limited English support.

Main charitable entity types: General incorporated association (一般社団法人); Specified NPO (特定非営利活動法人); Unincorporated voluntary group (任意団体)
Key local requirements: No nationality or residency bar — a foreign founder can serve as director — but registration requires a Japanese registered office address (serviced/registered-agent office works), Japanese-language articles, and a registered seal (hanko).
Est. cost & time: Government fees of roughly ¥30,000–50,000 plus office costs; a general incorporated association registers in about 2–4 weeks, while Specified-NPO certification takes 3–6 months.
Notes: The fastest expat path is the non-profit general incorporated association (can register in as little as two weeks); Specified-NPO status adds tax-deductible donation treatment but a longer, prefecture-run certification. All documents in Japanese; English support is limited.

Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (재단법인); Incorporated association (사단법인); Nonprofit corporation (비영리법인)
Key local requirements: Foreigners are permitted to establish foundations in Korea with no director-residency requirement; registration (district/city office under the Act on Incorporation of Associations and Foundations) needs a local office address, a Korean-language constitution, and for a foundation a minimum endowment commonly cited at 100 million won (~USD 70,000).
Est. cost & time: Low official registration fees; with a local agent typically a few weeks to ~2 months once endowment is in place.
Notes: Confirmed viable for expats (KOTRA/Invest Korea and formation guides both confirm foreigners can register foundations and NGOs); Korean-language paperwork is the main burden; popular expat-charity route is the 재단 법인 for grantmaking.

Main charitable entity types: Public-interest foundation (公募基金会); Non-public-interest foundation (非公募基金会); Private non-enterprise unit (民办非企业单位)
Key local requirements: Registration requires a Chinese supervising/competent unit (主管单位), a Chinese registered address, and a paid-in registered fund of at least 2 million RMB (public-interest foundation) or 800,000 RMB (non-public-interest); foreign individuals generally cannot directly sponsor these entities.
Est. cost & time: Several months to over a year including the 2-year operational-pilot requirement and approvals; official fees low, agent/legal costs significant.
Notes: Direct foreign formation is effectively barred without a local Chinese partner organization; foreign-funded groups must register under the Foreign NGO Law (2+ years of overseas track record) or operate through a local partner — heavy political/supervision risk, no English-language process.

Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (財團法人); Mutual-benefit association (互益社團法人)
Key local requirements: Foreigners can form a private foundation with a local registered office in Taiwan and a deposited minimum capital of 15 million NTD (local-level registration) or 30 million NTD (central-level, Ministry of the Interior); documents in Chinese, board can include foreign directors.
Est. cost & time: Modest registration fees (a few hundred to a few thousand USD with legal help); typically 4–12 weeks once capital is deposited.
Notes: The 財團法人 (foundation) is the standard expat charitable vehicle; formation guides confirm foreign founders are accepted and foreign staff may be hired; Chinese-language bureaucracy, no direct foreign-ownership ban.

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee (no share capital); Charitable trust under deed of trust; Registered society (small member groups)
Key local requirements: No nationality or residency requirement for directors/members; a Hong Kong registered office address (virtual office works) and company secretary must be in place; charity status for tax benefits is a separate application to the HK Jockey Club (HKJC).
Est. cost & time: Government incorporation fees of a few hundred to ~HK$2,000; incorporation in 3–5 days; HKJC charitable registration (for donation tax deductions) takes additional 1–3 months.
Notes: The most accessible route in this list; full English-language process; popular expat pathway is the company limited by guarantee, then HKJC charitable status; low political risk.

Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (Fundação Privada, Law 16/2021, in force 2022); Association (社團, new law in force 2022)
Key local requirements: No nationality bar; the foundation can be established by a single founder with a donated endowment and a local office address, via the DSAJ registration process (name certificate, then incorporation with Civil Affairs Bureau); an association requires a minimum of 7 founding members.
Est. cost & time: Notary and registration costs of a few hundred to a few thousand MOP; typically a few weeks to 2–3 months.
Notes: The 2021/2022 modernization (association and foundation laws) lowered formation barriers; documents in Chinese or Portuguese — English support is limited; political risk similar to Macau generally.

Main charitable entity types: Registered charity (Registrar of Charities), company incorporated by guarantee, society
Key local requirements: At least one director/trustee resident in Singapore, local registered office (agent address OK), English-language constitution.
Notes: No foreign-formation ban; English-language bureaucracy; most region-friendly setup; separate IRC tax-exempt (s16/s17) and PCDU applications follow incorporation.

Main charitable entity types: Society (Societies Act 1966), charitable trust, company incorporated by guarantee
Key local requirements: Local registered office, at least one local resident officer (company: resident director; society: Malaysian officebearers), English filings accepted.
Notes: Society is the common expat-charity form; registration in English or Bahasa; straightforward via local secretary/agent.

Main charitable entity types: Yayasan (foundation), perkumpulan (association)
Key local requirements: Individual foreign founder must have resided in Indonesia 5 consecutive years; foreign board members need Ministry of Foreign Affairs recommendation; local notary deed required.
Notes: Effectively foreigners use an Indonesian corporate (PT) or local individual as founder of record, or partner with an existing yayasan; Bahasa Indonesia dominant.

Main charitable entity types: Foundation (Foundation Act 2007), registered NGO/society, charitable trust
Key local requirements: Majority of foundation board Thai nationals, local registered office, Thai-language documents, in-person notarisation steps.
Notes: Most foreigners establish a foundation with all-Thai board and act as funder/advisor; high political sensitivity (NGO rules, lèse-majesté) — avoid politically active purposes.

Main charitable entity types: Social charity organisation (local NGO), INGO representative office
Key local requirements: Only Vietnamese social organisations can be formed; foreign individuals cannot found a local charity; INGO registration needs MFA/COMINGO approval and foreign funding source.
Est. cost & time: N/A for individual foreign founder (INGO route: 3–6 months)
Notes: Practical route is partnering with a Vietnamese social organisation or registering in Singapore; strict annual reporting; no local fundraising by INGOs.

Main charitable entity types: Non-stock non-profit corporation (SEC), charitable trust, association
Key local requirements: At least two-thirds of directors of a non-stock corporation must be Filipino citizens resident in the Philippines; trust trustees likewise Filipino; local office address.
Notes: English is an official language — filings in English; popular expat hub; common structure is a Filipino-majority board with the foreigner as incorporator/trust donor.

Main charitable entity types: Association, NGO (Law on Associations and NGOs 2003, as amended), foundation
Key local requirements: Founding members must be Cambodian nationals; local office and national chair; annual renewal and foreign-funding registration (MOFA) for INGO activity.
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 200 + local sponsor costs, 1–2 months if via Cambodian nationals)
Notes: 2025 draft/NGO law further tightens controls; notable political risk and periodic clampdowns on foreign-funded NGOs; partner with local nationals as founders of record.

Main charitable entity types: Social organisation (Law on Social Organisations and NGOs), INGO representative office
Key local requirements: Founding members must be Lao residents/nationals with a Lao national chair; local office; state registration via Ministry of Home Affairs.
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 100–300 + legal fees via local partners, 2–6 months)
Notes: Heavily state-controlled civil society; Lao language required; INGOs operate only through approved local partners and MFA authorisation.

Main charitable entity types: Registered charity/association (National Registration Bureau), INGO representative office
Key local requirements: Registration requires a local sponsor/contact and Burmese-language filings; foreign individuals cannot form organisations directly.
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 100–300 via local sponsor, months if feasible)
Notes: High political risk (civil war, sanctions, unstable NCA); most foreign charities operate via international partners or pre-2021 registered bodies only.

Main charitable entity types: Society (Societies Act), charitable trust (registered with Registrar of Societies)
Key local requirements: Local registered office, majority of office-bearers Bruneian citizens, in-person registry steps; no online filing.
Notes: Very small, closed registration culture aimed at locals; English is official so language is fine, but foreign-led charities are rare — most operate through existing local bodies.

Main charitable entity types: Association (2009 Law on Associations), NGO, foundation
Key local requirements: Physical local office, registered local address and national contact officer; filings in Tetum/Portuguese/English; slow manual process.
Notes: Foreign members are permitted under the 2009 law and INGOs do register here; bureaucracy is slow and requires a local agent; less predictable than Singapore/Malaysia.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust, company limited by guarantee (CLBG), registered association
Key local requirements: Australian resident (home jurisdiction); registered office in Australia; 2+ Australian-resident trustees/directors; ABN then ACNC registration for charitable status
Est. cost & time: A$0 ACNC fee (~A$514 if incorporating a CLBG with ASIC), 1-4 weeks
Notes: Home setup: register with ACNC (Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission) for tax-deductible-gift status; most foreign-linked founders use a charitable trust with local trustees

Main charitable entity types: Incorporated society, company limited by guarantee, registered trust
Key local requirements: Charity Commission registration (free, online); NZ-based charity board majority for tax status; no strict local-citizen rule for society incorporation
Notes: Very straightforward English-language process; foreign founders commonly use an incorporated society with some NZ-resident officers

Main charitable entity types: Charitable trust (registered trust), company limited by guarantee
Key local requirements: CLBG: 3 directors, 2 ordinarily resident in Fiji; charitable trust: 2+ trustees + local registered address; English widely used
Notes: Trusts registered with FRCS/Registrar; CLBG route is the common NGO structure; appointing two resident Fijian directors is the main hurdle

Main charitable entity types: Non-commercial company limited by guarantee, registered association (NGO)
Key local requirements: Resident company secretary in PNG; 7+ members with 3+ PNG residents for non-commercial company; local registered office
Notes: Bureaucracy heavy, English official language but processes slow; most international NGOs register via a PNG partner or use an Australian-registered entity operating cross-border

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee, registered trust
Key local requirements: At least 1 director resident in Samoa; local registered office/agent; 2+ trustees for a trust
Notes: Small registry, English official; foreign trustees allowed with a local resident officer; SIFA handles international structures (not for local charities)

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust, company (limited)
Key local requirements: Resident trustee/director and local office; registration with Ministry of Justice/trust registry
Notes: Small, insular bureaucracy; limited precedent for foreign-registered charities; political sensitivity around foreign NGOs - community consent often expected

Main charitable entity types: Company limited by guarantee, registered trust
Key local requirements: CLBG needs local registered office/agent; 1+ resident director recommended; English widely used
Notes: Relatively permissive offshore-friendly registry; post-2021 coup political risk noted by some aid donors

Main charitable entity types: Charitable trust (registered), company limited by guarantee
Key local requirements: Charitable trusts must be registered with charitable purpose; local registered office and resident officer recommended; 2+ trustees
Notes: English official, cooperative registry; foreign charitable trusts common (many Pacific-worker charities registered here); political instability occasional

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust, company (limited)
Key local requirements: Local registered office, resident trustee/director; small central registry in Tarawa
Notes: Very small registry with limited published process; English official but slow administration; few foreign charity registrations on record

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust, company (offshore IBC available)
Key local requirements: Minimal corporate framework; no established charitable registration regime; local agent required for any entity
Notes: No dedicated charity register; foreign founders can only form IBC/trust via offshore service providers; not a practical charity jurisdiction

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust, company
Key local requirements: Business registration effectively restricted to Tuvaluan citizens or Tuvalu-based businesses (per Ministry of Finance); local officers and office required
Notes: Explicit non-citizen registration restrictions; no practical foreign charity pathway; use a partner in Fiji/NZ instead

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust (trust company regime), company, LLC
Key local requirements: Local registered agent (default: The Trust Company of the Marshall Islands, Inc.) for non-residents; no local directors required for most entities
Notes: Well-developed English-language trust/registered-agent infrastructure; charitable purposes uncommon but trust structures easy to set up

Main charitable entity types: Registered trust, corporation/LLC (state-level)
Key local requirements: Registration in one of 4 states (or federally) with a local registered agent; no local-citizen director requirement
Notes: Small registries, English official; registered-agent services available; charitable framework informal - trust deed is the usual vehicle

Main charitable entity types: foundation (vakıf), association (dernek)
Key local requirements: Foreigner may found a vakıf only under legal/actual reciprocity (Australia has no treaty, so practice relies on case-by-case reciprocity finding); majority of foundation board members must be Turkey residents; a local registered office address is required.
Est. cost & time: US$500–1,500 with a Turkish lawyer, ~1–3 months
Notes: Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü (Foundation Directorate) handles vakıfs; dernek registration is cheaper and simpler (province governor's office, ~1 month). English paperwork accepted with sworn Turkish translation. Political/currency risk (lira volatility) is the main practical concern, not formation law.

Main charitable entity types: public benefit organization (მფარველობითი ორგანიზაცია), charitable foundation (სარგებლობის ფონდი), non-profit organization (NPO)
Key local requirements: Single founder (any nationality), a Georgian registered address (virtual/agent addresses accepted), no minimum funding.
Est. cost & time: ~GEL 25 (US$9) state fee, 3–10 business days, fully online
Notes: Registration via Public Service Development Agency portal; English-language interface and English filings accepted. Most user-friendly regime on this list; popular with foreigners. Watch 2024–25 political instability — no effect on registration itself, but banks may apply enhanced due diligence to new entities.

Main charitable entity types: public organization (հասարակական կազմակերպություն), foundation (հիմնադրամ)
Key local requirements: Foreign citizens may found NGOs; a local (Yerevan/Armenian) registered office is required; documents in Armenian (or Russian, widely accepted in practice).
Est. cost & time: Minimal state fee (~600 AMD, under US$2), ~10–15 business days
Notes: Registration via public services (e-gov) system; apostille/translation of foreign documents needed. Post-2020 South Caucasus realignment has not tightened NGO law; Armenia is one of the more open CIS-adjacent jurisdictions for foreigners.

Main charitable entity types: public association (ictimai birlik), foundation (fond)
Key local requirements: Foreign citizens may formally be founders of a fond, but all board/officer control must be locally resident; August 2025 amendments prohibit banking operations with foreign financial sources for NGOs and add heavy fines, effectively barring foreign-funded charities.
Est. cost & time: State fee modest (~1,000 AZN equivalent), but real-world processing 1–3+ months with high rejection risk
Notes: Azerbaijan is among the most restrictive NGO jurisdictions in Europe/Caucasus: repeated waves of 2024–2025 legislation on foreign funding, de-foreignization of the sector, and administrative fines. Even if a fond is registered, receiving Australian donor funds is practically blocked; political risk is extreme.

Main charitable entity types: public association (қоғамдық бірлестік / IiO non-profit partnership), foundation (қор)
Key local requirements: Foreign citizens can be founders (foreign legal persons generally cannot); a local registered address in Kazakhstan is required; filings in Kazakh (Russian accepted in practice).
Est. cost & time: Small state fee (~500–2,000 KZT), 5–10 business days via single-window registration
Notes: Registration with the Justice Committee/region. Kazakhstan's 2023 NGO reform simplified formation, but annual reporting and foreign-funding reporting obligations are strict. A Mongolian dual citizen faces no special preference — treated as a foreign founder.

Main charitable entity types: public organization (jamoat birligi), charitable foundation (xayriya jamg'armasi)
Key local requirements: Uzbek citizens must constitute a core of founders (a sole foreign founder is generally not acceptable for a jamoat birligi; a foundation allows a foreign founder with local participation); local registered office required; Uzbek-language filings.
Est. cost & time: Near-zero state fee, ~5 business days via one-stop window (2023 reform)
Notes: The 2023 Presidential Decree modernized NGO registration (simplified one-stop process, e-filing), making formation the easiest phase; ongoing supervision and foreign-funding disclosure remain tight. Use a local partner or registered agent; Russian widely accepted in business practice.

Main charitable entity types: public organization (köpagalyam birleşigi) — government-established only in practice
Key local requirements: NGOs can only be created with the explicit approval of the relevant state organ; there is no independent NGO registration path and no mechanism for a foreigner to found one.
Notes: Turkmenistan effectively has a state monopoly on civil society; no functioning independent charity sector, no English-language process, and no published cost/time. Not a viable jurisdiction for this founder; do not invest time here.

Main charitable entity types: public organization (jamoiy tashkilot), foundation (jamgarcha)
Key local requirements: Foreign citizens may be founders, but registration is in-person in Dushanbe (Ministry of Justice), requires Tajik/Russian-language documents, a local legal address, and notarized/apostilled paperwork.
Est. cost & time: Small state fee (~US$50–100), ~30 days, plus travel
Notes: Bureaucratic, Russian/Tajik-heavy process with no e-filing; NGOs operate under a restrictive environment (post-2024 crackdowns on civil society, 'foreign agent'-style pressure). Realistic only with a local law firm handling the file; political risk is significant.

Main charitable entity types: charitable fund (ылайыктуу фонд / karyte fund), public organization, association (assotsiatsiya)
Key local requirements: A fund can be founded by a single person of any nationality; a local registered address (agent addresses work); filings in Kyrgyz (Russian accepted; English with translation in practice).
Est. cost & time: State duty ~2,000 KGS (US$22), ~5 business days, e-filing via State Registration Portal
Notes: One of the easiest CIS registrations for a foreigner — a single-founder charitable fund with no local citizen requirement. Annual reporting and a local bank account required. Political volatility (2020, 2024) has not touched basic NGO registration law.

Main charitable entity types: non-governmental organization (tashkilat-e ghayre-hozoumi / NGO), public-benefit association (ettehadiye-ye khedmat-e ghalbeye mardom)
Key local requirements: Registration requires Ministry of Interior (and relevant ministry) approval under the 2005 NGO Law; in practice, only Iranian nationals with an aligned political/religious profile are approved, and a foreign founder's application is not a viable path.
Est. cost & time: Nominal state fee; process 6–12+ months with a near-certain refusal for a foreigner
Notes: All organizations must be compatible with the constitution and 'the tenets of the Islamic Republic'; independent civil society is heavily restricted and monitored (2024–25 further crackdowns). International sanctions (US/EU) make banking and funding an added hard blocker. Effectively not available to this founder; the standard workaround for Australians is a registered charity in an allied jurisdiction (e.g. Australia, Georgia, or Kyrgyzstan) operating cross-border.

Main charitable entity types: association loi (registered association); ONG agréée (accredited NGO)
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO requires prior Ministry of Interior authorization, a local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: 2017 civil-society law; heavy discretionary approval; most expats partner with an existing Cameroonian association instead.

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée; ONG agréée
Key local requirements: Government authorization for foreign associations, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: Conflict-affected with weak administration; security risk for on-ground work; few foreign NGOs operate legally.

Main charitable entity types: association loi; ONG agréée (2017 NGO law)
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO needs prior Ministry of Interior approval, resident legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: 2017 NGO law replaced the 1967 framework; political instability since 2020; approval is slow and discretionary.

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée; ONG accréditée
Key local requirements: Ministry of Interior accreditation (agrément) plus local legal representative and local office for foreign NGOs; filings in French.
Notes: French-language bureaucracy; accreditation is discretionary; stable enough for a registered agent/representative to work.

Main charitable entity types: ONG enregistrée; association; trust
Key local requirements: Congolese national legal representative is mandatory; foreign NGO approval from Ministry of Interior; local office.
Notes: Slow and heavily scrutinized; security risk in the east; most expats work through an established local partner.

Main charitable entity types: association loi; ONG agréée
Key local requirements: Ministry of Interior accreditation, local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: French-language process; post-2023 political transition adds uncertainty to approvals.

Main charitable entity types: asociación inscrita; ONG autorizada
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO authorization from Ministry of Interior, local representative and local office; filings in Spanish/French.
Notes: Highly centralized regime; approval is slow and discretionary; narrow civil-society space; Spanish (and French) bureaucracy.

Main charitable entity types: associação registada; ONG autorizada
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO authorization, local representative and local office; filings in Portuguese/French.
Notes: Very small, under-resourced administration; slow processing; few registered foreign NGOs; French/Portuguese required.

Main charitable entity types: NGO registered with MIDRRP (national NGO or foreign NGO)
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO needs 2+ years' existence abroad, a local partner and Rwandan legal representative; Rwandan majority board for national NGOs.
Notes: Strict, well-enforced 2016 NGO Act; English/French/Kinyarwanda; many expats operate through Rwandan partners rather than foreign registration.

Main charitable entity types: ONG agréée
Key local requirements: Prior approval from the Ministry of State for Humanitarian Affairs, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: Multiple foreign NGOs have been expelled; very high political risk; approvals are discretionary and often denied.

Main charitable entity types: NGO/CSO (local NGO or foreign NGO, NGO/CSO Act 2016)
Key local requirements: Local NGOs need a Ugandan majority board; foreign NGOs register with Ministry of Internal Affairs with a resident legal representative and must route funds via Ugandan bank accounts.
Notes: 2016 Act tightened foreign-funding rules; expats usually partner with a Ugandan-led CSO instead of foreign registration.

Main charitable entity types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act as amended); trust
Key local requirements: Two-thirds Tanzanian directors (2021 amendments); foreign-funded NGOs register with the NGO Commission; local office.
Notes: 2021 amendments tightened foreign-funding thresholds and local-content rules; English/Swahili; NGO Commission is strict.

Main charitable entity types: registered NGO (local organization or foreign organization, NGO Act 2003)
Key local requirements: Foreign organizations need resident Kenyan directors, a KES 100,000 bank deposit and NGO Commission registration; local office.
Notes: English-language, well-trodden expat route; many Australians register as foreign organizations; strong NGO infrastructure.

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée; ONG agréée (2019 NGO law)
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO approval from Ministry of Interior, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: Small islands, limited administrative capacity; political instability (2018 coup, 2024 elections); French required.

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée; ONG agréée
Key local requirements: Foreign NGOs accredited via Ministry of Foreign Affairs with a local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Notes: No local-citizenship board rule; political instability since 2023; French-language process, local agent usable.

Main charitable entity types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act 2005); trust
Key local requirements: Local NGOs need a Zambian majority on the board; local office; English filings.
Notes: Open, English, stable; expats commonly register local NGOs with Zambian directors; straightforward process.

Main charitable entity types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act 1997); trust
Key local requirements: Local NGOs need a Malawian majority (two-thirds) board; local office; English filings.
Notes: English-language, moderate bureaucracy; receiving foreign funds requires NGO registration.

Main charitable entity types: ONG nacional / ONG estrangeira (2005 NGO law)
Key local requirements: Foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with a Mozambican legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
Notes: Portuguese-language process; a hired local manager can serve as legal representative.

Main charitable entity types: associação registada; ONG with local representative
Key local requirements: Foreign NGO authorization from Ministry of Interior, local legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
Notes: Slow Portuguese-language bureaucracy; cautious approach needed for sensitive activities; few foreign charities register directly.

Main charitable entity types: registered NGO (NGO Act); trust
Key local requirements: Board of at least 3 members, local office and resident secretary; no citizenship restriction; English filings.
Notes: Stable, English-language; straightforward but small-bureaucracy processing times.

Main charitable entity types: non-profit society (Societies Act); public benefit trust (Deeds Registry)
Key local requirements: No local-director requirement; local registered office/agent and English filings.
Notes: English, registered agents widely available; a popular route for SADC-based charities; low regulatory burden.

Main charitable entity types: local/foreign NGO (NGO Act 2005); trust
Key local requirements: Local NGOs need a two-thirds Zimbabwean board; foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Local Government with a local representative; fees in USD.
Notes: Political risk and restrictions on donor funding for certain activities; English language; many NGOs operate via local partnerships.

Main charitable entity types: non-profit society (Societies Act); NGO (foreign-fund registration)
Key local requirements: Local office; registration with the Registrar of Societies plus NGO unit registration to receive foreign funds; English filings.
Notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; moderate small-country bureaucracy.

Main charitable entity types: non-profit society (Societies Act); trust
Key local requirements: Local office; registration with the Ministry of Justice; English filings.
Notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; slow small-bureaucracy processing.

Main charitable entity types: non-profit company (NPC, Companies Act); trust (Trust Property Control Act); PBO (SARS)
Key local requirements: No foreign restrictions; NCD online registration, local office/registered agent; English filings.
Notes: Most open route in the region; NPO/NPC + trust + PBO gives donor tax-deductibility; strong expat charity infrastructure and English.

Main charitable entity types: Stichting (foundation), Vereniging (association), ANBI-registered charity (tax status)
Key local requirements: No citizenship/residency requirement for founder or board; 1+ board member (stichting), Dutch registered office (virtual office acceptable), ANBI declaration to Belastingdienst
Notes: Most popular EU route for foreign founders; stichting + ANBI is the standard expat-charity path; board may be entirely non-resident; English-language guidance available; no minimum endowment

Main charitable entity types: ASBL/ISP/VOG (non-profit association), Stichting/Fondation (foundation)
Key local requirements: Belgian registered office (seat must be in Belgium); association requires 1+ founder (since 2024 reform), 3+ traditionally; foundation requires EUR 25,000 minimum capital; French/Dutch-language statutes
Notes: ASBL is the standard vehicle and easy via a local registered-office provider; AIT tax-exempt status is a separate application; French-speaking practice dominates; no in-person steps required

Main charitable entity types: Association (1912 law), Fondation (2003 law), European non-profit association (ENPA)
Key local requirements: Luxembourg registered office; association needs 3+ founding members; foundation requires EUR 100,000 minimum endowment (Art. 40(3)) and court authorisation; English widely accepted
Est. cost & time: EUR 200-600 for association, 1-4 weeks; foundation several months (Tribunal authorisation)
Notes: Most English-friendly EU jurisdiction; charitable income exempt from tax; foundation route is capital-heavy, association is the practical expat choice

Main charitable entity types: Association loi 1901, Fonds de dotation, Fondation reconnue d'utilité publique
Key local requirements: Association needs 2+ named founders (practically a president + 1 officer), French registered office; fond de dotation requires EUR 15,000 minimum endowment; French-language declaration at préfecture
Est. cost & time: Association: free (déclaration), 1-2 weeks; fonds de dotation: EUR 15,000 endowment + EUR 300-500 filing
Notes: Association 1901 is quick and free; tax-exempt status (Art. 64 ter CGI) is complex and separate; French required in practice; public-utility recognition requires ~EUR 1M endowment and decree

Main charitable entity types: Eingetragener Verein (e.V.), Gemeinnützige gGmbH, Private foundation (Stiftung, state law)
Key local requirements: e.V. needs 7+ founding members, German registered office (Geschäftssitz in Germany), German-language articles; foreign founders/directors allowed without residency proof
Notes: e.V. is the standard vehicle; charity status (gemeinnützig) confirmed later by Finanzamt; state register courts are slow; foundation endowments vary by state from ~EUR 10,000-25,000

Main charitable entity types: Eingetragener Verein (Verein), Private foundation (Stiftung, state-level law)
Key local requirements: Verein needs 3+ founders, Austrian seat (local address), Austrian-language articles; no citizenship requirement for founders or board
Notes: Verein is the practical vehicle; foundation laws are state-by-state (Landesrecht) with endowments from ~EUR 30,000-75,000; German required; charity tax recognition via Finanzamt

Main charitable entity types: Stiftung/Foundation, Verein/Association (Swiss Civil Code)
Key local requirements: Foundation requires CHF 50,000 minimum capital, Swiss seat, 3+ foundation council members with at least 1 Swiss-domiciled; association needs 3+ founders and a Swiss board seat
Est. cost & time: Foundation: CHF 50,000 endowment + CHF 1,000-2,000 registration, 4-8 weeks; association: CHF 500-1,000, 1-4 weeks
Notes: No citizenship requirement for founders; Swiss-resident officer is the key hurdle (use local agent); trilingual; neutral-content requirement for foundations; no formal 'charity' register - exemption via tax authority

Main charitable entity types: Anstiftung (private foundation, 2013 law), Verein (association)
Key local requirements: Foundation requires CHF 30,000 minimum endowment, seat in Liechtenstein, managing board seated locally (local officer/agent needed); German-language filings
Notes: Small, stable, English-tolerant jurisdiction; local board presence makes it impractical without a local agent; no formal charity register; often paired with Swiss structures

Main charitable entity types: Fondation (sovereign decree), Association (sovereign declaration)
Key local requirements: Foundation requires EUR 50,000 minimum endowment and discretionary decree of the Prince on advice of the foundations commission; Monégasque registered office; French-language filings
Notes: No formal charity category - establishment is discretionary sovereign approval; French required; popular with high-net-worth founders; no corporate income tax; in-person steps common

Main charitable entity types: Fondazione (foundation), Associazione (association)
Key local requirements: San Marino registered office; Italian-language filings; small opaque bureaucracy with in-person steps; endowment set by founding act for foundations
Notes: Tiny jurisdiction with few foreign precedents and no English-language service; most foreigners use a neighbouring Italian (Emilia-Romagna) association instead; Italian required

Main charitable entity types: Fundació (foundation, Law 14/2003), Associació (non-profit association)
Key local requirements: Foundation requires endowment of at least EUR 100,000 per founding act, Andorran seat, local management presence; Catalan/Spanish-language filings, notarised documents
Notes: Popular with affluent founders seeking a European low-tax base; high endowment and local-presence requirements make it hard for a remote foreign founder; Catalan required in practice

Main charitable entity types: fundacja (foundation), stowarzyszenie (association), public benefit organization (pożytk pożyteczna organizacja, POUS)
Key local requirements: Fundacja needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed, no citizenship requirement), a notarized deed and a local registered office; association needs 7+ members.
Est. cost & time: ~500-1,500 PLN notary + small fees; ~2-4 weeks (statutory 30 days)
Notes: Most expat-friendly route in the region; separate 'benefit organization' (OPP) listing gives charity tax benefits; good English-language legal market.

Main charitable entity types: spolek (association), obecně užitečná korporace (OUK, public benefit corporation), nadace (foundation)
Key local requirements: Spolek needs 5+ members (foreigners allowed), a local registered office; OUK needs 1 founder, ~100,000 CZK endowment, notary deed; Czech-language statute.
Est. cost & time: Spolek: registration free + notary ~1,000-2,500 CZK; ~4-8 weeks; OUK faster (~2-4 weeks)
Notes: Digital registry, straightforward; public-benefit (obecně prospěšná) tax status is a separate Ministry of Interior approval.

Main charitable entity types: nezisková organizácia (nonprofit organization), verejne prospešná organizácia (VPO), nadácia (foundation)
Key local requirements: Organization needs 2+ founders, local office and Slovak-language charter; foundation via notarized deed, endowment per charter; no citizenship requirement.
Notes: VPO public-benefit status is a separate Ministry of Interior procedure; Slovak language barrier; paperwork moderate.

Main charitable entity types: civil nonprofit szervezet (civil nonprofit organization), nonprofit kft (nonprofit limited company), alapítvány (foundation)
Key local requirements: Nonprofit organization needs 2+ members (foreigners allowed); foundation 1 founder + charter, Hungarian-language deed, local office.
Est. cost & time: Nonprofit org: low/no state fee + notary ~30,000-60,000 HUF, ~2-4 weeks; nonprofit kft needs 3,000,000 HUF capital
Notes: Foreign-funded NGOs above a threshold (~300M HUF/yr) need government authorization (Stop-Soros legacy) — politically sensitive; public-benefit (közhasznú) status is a separate, stricter regime.

Main charitable entity types: združenje (association, javno koristno status), fundacija (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ members (foreigners allowed), local office, Slovenian-language charter; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Est. cost & time: Association ~200-500 EUR, ~1-2 months; foundation ~1,000-3,000 EUR, ~1-3 months
Notes: Public-benefit (javno koristno) status is a separate procedure with membership-base criteria; English support limited outside Ljubljana.

Main charitable entity types: udruga (association, javno korisna status), zakladnica (foundation), neprofitna ustanova (nonprofit institution)
Key local requirements: Udruga needs 3+ founding members (foreigners allowed), local office, Croatian-language statutes, notarized application in 2 copies.
Est. cost & time: ~500-1,500 HRK fees + notary; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days, often longer)
Notes: EU e-government decent; javno korisna (public-benefit) status is a separate Ministry of Interior step; many expats use a local legal/NGO-service provider.

Main charitable entity types: udruženje/udruga (association), fundacija (foundation)
Key local requirements: 3+ founders, local office, charter in local language; registration happens at entity level (Republika Srpska vs Federation of BiH), sometimes municipal, so structure depends on where the office is.
Est. cost & time: ~100-300 BAM (very low); ~2-6 weeks per tier, can stretch to months
Notes: Three-layer state/entity system creates duplicated paperwork; no online registry; English support rare; foreign founders allowed but bureaucracy heavy.

Main charitable entity types: udruženje građana (citizens' association), fundacija (foundation), neprofitna ustanova (nonprofit institution)
Key local requirements: Association needs 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Serbian-language charter; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Notes: Non-EU; English support limited; cheap registration; foreign founders routinely register (many Serbian diaspora do this); apostille for foreign ID documents.

Main charitable entity types: udruženje građana (citizens' association), fundacija (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Montenegrin-language charter; no online registry, in-person/notarized steps.
Notes: Slow bureaucracy, documents in Montenegrin, minimal English support; EU-candidate so framework is straightforward in principle.

Main charitable entity types: udruženje (association), fundacija (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Macedonian-language charter; low fees.
Notes: EU candidate, cheap and low-bureaucracy; language barrier for a resident-in-Australia founder means using a local agent/lawyer.

Main charitable entity types: bashkimi (association), themelimin (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Albanian-language charter; new 2021 electronic register accepts applications by post/courier.
Notes: 2021 NPO registration law modernized the register; English support limited; foreign-founded NGOs common, often with local partners.

Main charitable entity types: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language charter (Russian widely used in practice); foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Notes: Cheap; EU candidate; political/economic volatility and weak enforcement; banking for foreign directors can be fiddly.

Main charitable entity types: publichna organizatsiia (public organization), fundatsiia (foundation), publichno-koristna (public-benefit) status
Key local requirements: Organization 2+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Ukrainian-language documents (English with certified translation); state-fee registration online.
Est. cost & time: State duty ~1,000-2,500 UAH + translations/notary; ~1-2 weeks (online filing)
Notes: Registration itself is cheap and fast, but active war, banking/sanctions friction for a foreign resident founder and currency risk make this a risky base; many Western expat charities run via local Ukrainian partners.

Main charitable entity types: publicnaya organizatsiya (public organization), fundatsiya (foundation)
Key local requirements: Nominally 5+ members for an organization (foreigners allowed in statute), local office, Belarusian-language charter; in practice foreign-funded NGOs above a funding threshold must register as 'undesirable organizations' before operating.
Est. cost & time: Nominally low fees, 1-3 months; in practice effectively barred for an independent foreign founder
Notes: 2021+ crackdown on independent civil society; heavy political risk; private foundations rare and state-dominated; not recommended for this founder.

Main charitable entity types: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
Est. cost & time: ~500 RON state fee + notary ~1,000-2,000 RON; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days)
Notes: EU member; moderate bureaucracy; 'de utilitate publică' (public-benefit) tax status is a separate, stricter procedure; English support OK in Bucharest/Cluj.

Main charitable entity types: shtoprofitna asotsiia (public-benefit association), neprofitna pravno lice (nonprofit legal entity), fondatsiya (foundation)
Key local requirements: Nonprofit legal entity (NPL) needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed) + local office; association needs 5+ founders; Bulgarian-language documents.
Notes: EU member; the 1-founder NPL form is the simplest for a lone foreign founder; good English support in Sofia; cheap to operate.

Main charitable entity types: syndesmos (association, general-benefit status), themelioma (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association needs 5+ founders (foreigners allowed), Greek registered office, Greek-language charter filed with notary and court registry; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
Notes: 2019 law modernized foundations, but process is paper/notary-heavy, Greek language required, no meaningful online registry; use a local lawyer.

Main charitable entity types: charitable trust (unregistered), registered body (association), community chest
Key local requirements: A charitable trust needs only a settlor + trustee and no registration; registered body needs 3+ members (foreigners allowed) + local address; English fully accepted.
Est. cost & time: Trust: ~500-2,000 EUR via solicitor, days; registered body: ~100-500 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
Notes: English common-law jurisdiction — most expats set up a simple charitable trust with a Cypriot trustee; tax deductibility requires income-tax authority approval and a Cypriot public-benefit nexus; strong English-language professional services.

Main charitable entity types: association (2021 Non-Not-For-Profit Organisations Act), foundation, charitable trust
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local registered address; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed; English fully accepted.
Est. cost & time: Association ~150-500 EUR, ~days-2 weeks (online); foundation ~1,500-5,000 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
Notes: English official language, streamlined 2021 framework; foundation is the stronger form for asset-holding; charitable trusts available under trust law without registration.

Main charitable entity types: Registered charity (Charity Commission for Ireland), company limited by guarantee (CRO), unincorporated charitable trust
Key local requirements: Irish registered office and at least one EU-resident director/trustee; charities with income over €50k/yr must be registered with the Charity Commission for Ireland
Est. cost & time: CRO company ~€100 + CCI registration free; ~4–8 weeks
Notes: English-language, common-law system; no nationality requirement for trustees; most overseas founders set up a company limited by guarantee with a local registered-office agent, then register the charity

Main charitable entity types: Registered charity (Charity Commission England & Wales), company limited by guarantee, charitable trust
Key local requirements: Charity must be established and managed in the UK: UK address, UK-based board control, and in practice at least one UK-resident trustee; no citizenship requirement
Est. cost & time: CLG at Companies House ~£12; Charity Commission registration free; ~8–12 weeks
Notes: English-language, common law; the most popular expat-charity pathway; overseas individuals may be trustees provided management and control are in the UK

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit association (félag), foundation (stofnun), branch of foreign nonprofit (no formal 'charity' status)
Key local requirements: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation requires ~ISK 3m endowment and Icelandic management
Notes: Documents in Icelandic; tax exemption (reykjafrjálsefni) must be applied for separately with the tax office; small bureaucracy but limited English support

Main charitable entity types: Unincorporated nonprofit association (ideell organisasjon), foundation (stiftelse), branch of foreign NGO
Key local requirements: Norwegian address for the association (min. 3 adult members, no nationality rules); foundation needs ~NOK 1m capital and Norwegian-resident management
Notes: Online via Altinn with English available; association is simple but requires a local contact; foundations have strict Norwegian-control rules

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit association (yhdistys), foundation (säätiö)
Key local requirements: Finnish address; association needs min. 5 adult members; foundation needs €10k minimum capital, Finnish purpose, Finnish/Swedish-language operations and a Finnish-resident board
Notes: Finnish-language requirement for documents and minutes; PRH bureaucracy is the main burden; foundations are hard for a foreign founder

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit association (ideell förening), foundation (stiftelse)
Key local requirements: Swedish registered seat (säte) and min. 3 members for the association, no residency requirement; foundation needs ~SEK 250k+ and a Swedish-resident board
Notes: Straightforward online registration with Bolagsverket, English widely understood; a Swedish bank account for the entity typically requires a personal/D-number for the signatory

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit association (forening), foundation (stiftelse), nonprofit company
Key local requirements: Danish address, min. 2 members, registered in the CVR register; 2023 Foundation Act requires Danish-controlled foundations (Danish-resident board majority)
Notes: Association name and documents must be in Danish; CVR registration itself is easy; Danish-controlled foundation rules make the foundation route hard for a foreigner

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit association (ühing/selts), nonprofit foundation (sihtasutus)
Key local requirements: Estonian registered address (virtual office available); association needs min. 5 members, no nationality rules; foundation needs a small endowment (~€2,600+)
Notes: 100% online e-Business Register with English available; no local-national requirement; among the easiest jurisdictions for a foreign founder

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit organization (NVO, unified 2016-law form), foundation (dibinājums), religious organization
Key local requirements: Latvian address, Latvian-language name/documents, and founding documents notarized by a Latvian notary before registration with the Enterprise Register
Est. cost & time: State fee ~€30–100 plus notary costs; ~1–2 months
Notes: The 2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law unified the forms; the notary step forces an in-person visit or a local representative, which is the main barrier for a foreign founder

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit organization (NVO), public benefit institution (viešoji įstaiga), foundation
Key local requirements: Lithuanian address, Lithuanian-language name and documents; NVO needs a board and min. 1–2 founders; registration via e-signature or notary with the Register of Legal Entities
Est. cost & time: State fee ~€20–50 (plus notary if offline); ~3–10 business days
Notes: The fully online route requires a Lithuanian e-ID, so a foreign founder usually acts through a local notary or representative; otherwise the process is fast

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (unincorporated association), plus limited charitable societies (SL/SA with statutory purpose)
Key local requirements: Spanish registered office (domicilio social), Spanish-resident legal representative (representante legal), notarial deed of incorporation, and a minimum endowment of ~€30,000 for a fundación
Est. cost & time: €1,500–€3,500 total (notary, registry, legal fees); ~1–3 months including regional foundation registry
Notes: Foreign founders can establish a fundación without Spanish nationality or tax residency; the practical hurdle is appointing a resident legal representative and local office (via a Spanish firm/registered agent). Fundaciones register in the regional foundation registry (Registro de Fundaciones) of the relevant autonomous community, so timelines and minor fees vary by region. English is not an official language for filings; all documents must be in Spanish with sworn translations where needed. No citizenship requirement, so with a local counsel/agent it is manageable.

Main charitable entity types: Fundação (private foundation, public-interest institution), Associação (association), and Instituto (institute)
Key local requirements: Portuguese registered office and a locally-based responsible party/director; the foundation deed (estatutos) must be notarised; no statutory minimum endowment, but the granting authority can require a material contribution sufficient for the object to be deemed of public interest
Est. cost & time: €1,000–€2,500 (notary, legal, fees); ~1–2 months for notarisation and public-interest status
Notes: The most straightforward of the four for a foreign founder: no citizenship/residency requirement for the founder, and no fixed minimum capital. However, to be treated as an entity of public interest (required for tax-exempt status and grants) it needs an endowment and approval by the relevant authority. English filings are not routine; use a Portuguese lawyer. A local office can be provided by a law firm or registered agent, which is what keeps this at medium rather than easy.

Main charitable entity types: Fondazione (private foundation), Associazione (unincorporated association), and cooperative sociale (social cooperative)
Key local requirements: Italian registered office, a founder who may be foreign (no citizenship/residency requirement), and a minimum endowment of €150,000 (fully paid at formation) for a fondazione; registration in the Third-Sector National Register (RUNTS)
Est. cost & time: €3,000–€6,000 professional costs plus the €150,000 endowment; ~2–4 months for notarisation, court filing and RUNTS entry
Notes: Foreign (including Australian) founders can legally establish a fondazione — explicitly no nationality or residency requirement — but the €150,000 fully-contributed endowment is the main barrier and makes it one of the costlier routes. Charitable status requires registration in RUNTS (Registro Unico Nazionale del Terzo Settore); the procedure is document-based and can be handled by a local lawyer with a representative, avoiding in-person steps. Italian-language filings are mandatory; English is not accepted for registry documents. The higher endowment and bureaucracy keep it at medium despite the permissive foreign-founder rule.

Main charitable entity types: No ordinary commercial/charitable registry; charitable activity is conducted through pontifical institutions, canonically erected entities, or bodies recognised by the Holy See (e.g., pontifical foundations/works) rather than a self-service registration
Key local requirements: No independent self-registration pathway; any entity operating on Vatican territory must be recognised/erected by the Holy See (competent dicastery/pontifical authority) and be compliant with the Fundamental Law of the Vatican City State
Est. cost & time: No fixed fee or standard timeline; entirely case-by-case at the discretion of the Holy See
Notes: The Vatican does not operate a conventional commercial-law or charity-registration framework open to foreign founders. There is no public registry an Australian-resident can simply file into. Charitable or philanthropic activity on Vatican territory is established by canonical/pontifical act (e.g., erection or recognition of a pontifical work), which requires a direct relationship with the appropriate Holy See authority and is typically reserved for Church-linked bodies. For a private foreign founder there is effectively no independent, self-service charitable-entity route; the realistic option is to establish the charity in Italy (or elsewhere) and, if relevant, seek a canonical relationship with the Holy See.

Main charitable entity types: amuta (registered association), nonprofit corporation (amuta atzmit), public-benefit corporation (charitable amuta with DSD status)
Key local requirements: 2-3 founders over 18 (Israeli citizenship NOT required), local Israeli registered agent/office, attorney-filed founding declaration and bylaws; English widely accepted
Notes: One of the most foreign-friendly registration regimes in the region; most foreign founders use an amuta plus a local managing director and registered-agent service; English-language filings routinely accepted; charity tax status (DSD/13-b) is a separate follow-up application

Main charitable entity types: registered association (jam'iyya) with Ministry of Social Affairs, charitable trust (less common)
Key local requirements: Board members must be Jordanian citizens, 18+, fully competent; Jordanian local address; Arabic documents; foreign founder can only be a non-board supporter
Est. cost & time: A$100-500 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding 5+ Jordanian-citizen board members)
Notes: Most foreigners fund through established Jordanian charities (e.g. JRC) or a branch/representative office instead of forming; government approval of bylaws and activities required; English not required in filings

Main charitable entity types: association (jama'iyya) under Law 92/1996, private foundation (muassasa khassisa)
Key local requirements: Foreigners CAN be founders and directors (no nationality rule) but need a local registered office, Arabic founding documents, and a local signatory; notification (declaration) regime, not pre-approval
Notes: Legally one of the easiest for foreigners in the region, but heavy Arabic-only bureaucracy, bank-account opening friction, and macro instability (currency, banking) make practical setup harder; most internationals use a local registered partner or a foundation

Main charitable entity types: association registered with Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, private foundation
Key local requirements: Local registration, local address and signatories; new association regime post-2025 is still being implemented; in-person steps in Syria; OFAC sanctions complicate cross-border funding and US-dollar transactions
Est. cost & time: Nominally low fees, 1-4 months in a stable environment; currently not practically achievable remotely
Notes: Civil-society registration resumed after 2025 transition (586 NGOs registered by Feb 2025) but framework unstable; sanctions exposure for foreign founders and their banks; English support effectively unavailable; advise against direct formation

Main charitable entity types: NGO/association (jam'iyya) under Law 12/2010, private foundation, branch of international NGO
Key local requirements: Founding members must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq-resident; minimum 10 founders; local board, local address; Arabic filings; activity approvals from MoSAL
Notes: Resident-expat route is the standard workaround (Iraqi-resident staff as founders); foreign funding rules restrict donor channels; English commonly understood in NGO sector but filings in Arabic; security considerations for in-person steps

Main charitable entity types: civil society organization (association) under the 2024 Civil Society Law, branch of foreign NGO (via partnership)
Key local requirements: At least 10 founding members, ALL Saudi citizens; Saudi board; Saudi address; no foreign-founded charities; foreigners may only join as members of an existing Saudi organization
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); partnership route: several months
Notes: New 2024 law (Royal Decree M/111) modernized the regime but kept the Saudi-citizenship floor; the only realistic foreign route is a program partnership with a Saudi charity or a representative office for an existing foreign NGO; English widely used in government dealings

Main charitable entity types: association (jam'iyya) under the NGOs Law, representative office of foreign NGO
Key local requirements: Founders and board must be Kuwaiti citizens; local address; Arabic filings; foreign individuals cannot form an NGO
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); representative-office route: 2-4 months with a local partner
Notes: Closed to foreign formation; foreigners work through established Kuwaiti charities (e.g. Kuwait Foundation for the Disabled, local societies) or a government-approved representative office; English usable informally, filings in Arabic

Main charitable entity types: private charitable institution (Qatar Charity framework), branch/partnership with an existing charity
Key local requirements: Founding of a charitable institution requires Qatari citizens (Qatari chair and majority); foreign founders cannot establish a standalone charity; English filings accepted by many agencies
Est. cost & time: N/A for foreign founder (standalone formation not permitted); partnership route: 1-3 months
Notes: 2023 philanthropy law tightened state oversight of foreign-funded work; standard foreign route is a partnership with Qatar Charity or an established Doha NGO, or a representative office approved by the relevant ministry

Main charitable entity types: private foundation (charitable) under Federal Decree-Law 11/2018, registered charity (DCC/DED charity license), association (jama'iyya) under FDL 2/2019
Key local requirements: Foundation: 1-3 founders, 100% foreign ownership allowed, AED 100,000+ capital, local service provider; association: board must be at least 70% UAE nationals; local office address; English accepted
Est. cost & time: Foundation: AED 30,000-75,000 all-in (capital + fees + agent), 4-8 weeks; DCC charity registration for an existing foreign charity: AED 5,000-15,000, 4-8 weeks
Notes: Most accessible Gulf option for a foreign founder: a UAE private foundation can be 100% foreign-held and run charitable activities; Dubai Charities (DCC) also registers existing international charities; the association route is blocked for all-foreign boards by the 70% nationality rule; strong English-language support

Main charitable entity types: association (jama'iyya), private foundation, branch of foreign NGO
Key local requirements: Founders and board majority must be Omani nationals; Omani chair; local address; Arabic filings; foreign founders cannot chair
Est. cost & time: A$200-600 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding Omani board members)
