Notes: Omani nationals are required for leadership roles; practical route for an Australian founder is a program partnership with an existing Omani charity or a representative office with a local sponsor; English usable in government dealings, filings in Arabic

Main charitable entity types: association (NGO) under Law 19/2006, branch of international NGO
Key local requirements: Founders must be Bahraini citizens (min. ~20) and board must be at least two-thirds Bahraini; local address; Arabic filings
Est. cost & time: A$200-500 fees, 4-8 weeks (gated by Bahraini board)
Notes: Bahrain is the most English-friendly and transparent NGO administration in the Gulf, but the nationality floor on founders/board keeps foreign formation out of reach; standard route is a partnership with an existing Bahraini NGO; government relations are comparatively accessible

Main charitable entity types: association (jama'iyya) under NGO Law 73/1991, NGO representative office (MOU-based)
Key local requirements: Registration with Ministry of Social Affairs, local address and local signatories; in-person steps; operating environment requires MOU with authorities
Est. cost & time: N/A in practice; formal route nominally 1-3 months in a stable environment, not feasible given the conflict
Notes: Civil war, fragmented governance, sanctions (Yemen Sanctions) and funding restrictions make direct foreign formation impractical; all foreign work runs through humanitarian MOUs with recognized authorities and established local partners; advise against

Main charitable entity types: registered society (jam'iyya) under the 1996 Societies Law, private foundation, branch of international NGO
Key local requirements: Minimum ~15 founders, two-thirds Palestinian residents of the area; local (Ramallah/West Bank) address; board majority local; Arabic filings; MoSAL registration in person
Est. cost & time: A$150-500 fees, 2-6 weeks in a normal environment; occupation/sanctions add friction
Notes: No local-partner requirement to register, so foreign participation in a society is legally possible, but in-person registration in Ramallah, movement/sanctions friction (OFAC Palestinian Territory guidelines) and banking constraints dominate; most foreigners operate via established local NGOs (e.g. PCHR, PNA partners) or international-NGO branch registration

Main charitable entity types: Association (Jam'iyya, Law 84/2014), private charitable institution (Law 149/2014), nonprofit company
Key local requirements: Local registered office, Egyptian-national founders/chair in practice, ministry (Youth & Sports / Social Solidarity) approval, Arabic documents.
Est. cost & time: EGP 1,000–5,000 (~US$20–100) + legal/agent fees, 3–6 months incl. security vetting
Notes: Heavy bureaucracy and security review; Arabic mandatory; many foreign-supported charities operate via local partner bodies or branches.

Main charitable entity types: Registered association (Jamiyya, 2005 civil society law)
Key local requirements: Sudanese founders/chair, local office, Ministry of Culture & Information approval.
Est. cost & time: ~US$100–300, 3–6 months, largely suspended due to conflict
Notes: 2023 civil war has paralysed registration bodies in most areas; acute security risk for foreign personnel; effectively unworkable right now.

Main charitable entity types: Registered association (Jam'iyya, Law 12/1989 as amended)
Key local requirements: Libyan-national founders/chair, local office, ministry approval; registry split between rival governments in Tripoli and the east.
Notes: Fragmented dual-government structure, militia influence, no workable foreign-formation path; foreign NGOs operate via UN/embassy channels only.

Main charitable entity types: Declared association (Law 12-06/2012 on associations, amended 2020)
Key local requirements: Local registered office, Arabic founding documents, declaration to the wilaya (provincial) authority; foreign founders heavily restricted.
Notes: Strict regulation with security vetting for any foreign involvement; slow bureaucracy; Arabic required.

Main charitable entity types: Declared association (1959 law, amended 2011)
Key local requirements: Registered office in Tunisia plus a local-resident representative (Tunisian, or foreigner resident in Tunisia); simple declaration to the prefecture.
Notes: Most open civil-society law in the region; declaration-based, so registration is fast; post-2022 political centralisation adds compliance risk.

Main charitable entity types: Association (Law 1956 on association rights), nonprofit company (SPA)
Key local requirements: Moroccan registered office, Arabic statutes, wilaya/provincial governor approval; foreign founders permitted.
Notes: Governor discretion can delay approvals; most expats register via a local address agent; Arabic mandatory.

Main charitable entity types: Association (1965 Code of Associations)
Key local requirements: Local registered office, meaningful local-national involvement, registration with the interior ministry; French/Arabic documents.
Notes: Very opaque, low-information bureaucracy; few foreign-led charities operate domestically; French-language burden.

Main charitable entity types: None (no independent registry; Moroccan association law applies in Moroccan-administered areas)
Key local requirements: Not available independently; the practical route is registering an association in Morocco.
Notes: Contested territory (Morocco vs. Polisario); no functioning independent civil-society registry; register in Morocco instead.

Main charitable entity types: Ethiopian charitable organization (2021 NGO Proclamation), foreign NGO office via a local partner
Key local requirements: Ethiopian-national founders for a domestic entity; a foreign founder must work through a partner organization or as a registered foreign NGO.
Notes: 2021 reform liberalised funding and registration, but foreigners cannot directly form a domestic charity; security clearance applies; Amharic/English documents.

Main charitable entity types: None (no independent NGO law; state-controlled associations only)
Key local requirements: No legal pathway for an independent foreign-founded charity.
Notes: No legal space for independent civil society; all associations are state-controlled; high political risk.

Main charitable entity types: Association (1971 law, as amended)
Key local requirements: Local registered office, Djiboutian-national chair/meaningful involvement, interior-ministry registration; French/Arabic documents.
Notes: Tight, security-driven regulation in a small country; English sometimes tolerated in practice; foreign aid actors mostly work through local partners.

Main charitable entity types: Registered charitable organization/NGO (2013 federal NGO law)
Key local requirements: Somali founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register through embassy channel; local presence and security plan required.
Notes: Severe insecurity and fragmented federal registries (Puntland, Somaliland, South West each have their own); foreign staff face high security risk.

Main charitable entity types: Registered association/NGO (2005 NGO law)
Key local requirements: Local registered office and local partner involvement, registration with the interior/social-affairs ministry.
Notes: De facto state without international recognition: banking, sanctions-compliance and repatriation risk; the civil-society registry is relatively functional and stable.

Main charitable entity types: Registered NGO (2009 NGO Act, amended 2018), domestic association
Key local requirements: South Sudanese founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register via embassy channel; local office required.
Notes: Post-conflict, high security risk, weak institutions; most international actors work through established partners or missions.

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit organization (Non-Profit Organizations Act 2013), public-benefit foundation, non-profit limited company
Key local requirements: Local registered office and licensed local agent; foreign directors permitted; registration with the Registrar of Companies.
Notes: English-language, simple, offshore-friendly regime; popular with foreign founders; a Seychelles charity gains no local tax-exempt status without local operations.

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit organization (NPO Act 2003), IFSA non-profit foundation, non-profit limited company
Key local requirements: Mauritian registered office (local agent provides it); foreign founders/directors permitted; NPOs have a local-presence element.
Notes: English-language with strong professional-services infrastructure; the IFSA foundation is the most foreigner-friendly route; popular expat-charity pathway.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (state trust deeds), registered society, Section 8 company (Companies Act 2013)
Key local requirements: Trust: 2+ trustees with at least one Indian-resident trustee in practice, Indian registered office and bank account; Sec 8 company: 1+ director resident in India 182 days/yr.
Est. cost & time: Trust: ~INR 2,000-15,000 fees plus stamp duty, 2-6 weeks; Sec 8: ~INR 30,000-50,000, 6-12 weeks
Notes: 12A (income-tax exemption) and 80G (donor deductions) registrations are separate follow-up applications, add 1-3 months. English widely used in filings. Foreign founders routinely use trust + Indian resident trustees.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (trust deed), Section 21 non-profit company (Companies Act 2017), registered society
Key local requirements: 2+ trustees with at least one Pakistani resident in practice, local registered office; Sec 21 company needs at least one Pakistani resident director and local secretary.
Notes: Tax-exempt status is a separate FBR application after incorporation. English used in filings; local resident trustee/director is the main hurdle for a foreign founder.

Main charitable entity types: NGO registered under the NGO Act 1961, charitable trust, registered society
Key local requirements: At least two-thirds of the NGO board must be Bangladeshi citizens (NGO Act 1961, s.3); local office and local officers required.
Notes: Foreign founder cannot form an NGO without enough Bangladeshi citizens to fill 2/3 of the board. The 2016 NGO Ordinance restricts foreign-funded NGOs (derogatory-remarks clause) - ongoing political/legal risk for donor-funded charities.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (registered with Registrar of Companies), society (Societies Ordinance), non-profit company
Key local requirements: Trust deed with 2+ registered persons (3 recommended), local registered office; no citizenship requirement for trustees.
Notes: Most expat-friendly in the region for a foreign founder; English is an official language. 12B tax-exempt status application to IRD follows trust registration.

Main charitable entity types: Trust (Trust Act 2064), NGO (NGO Registration Act 2049, District Administration Office), registered society
Key local requirements: NGO: board of 7 with at least 5 Nepali citizens, registration at the District Administration Office plus Social Welfare Council affiliation; Trust: 1+ settlor, foreign settlor permitted.
Notes: The trust route is the simplest expat pathway (no citizen-quota for trust deed). Foreign funding requires Social Welfare Council approval, which adds time and discretion.

Main charitable entity types: NGO (NGO Act 2008 / NGO Trust Act 1997), trust
Key local requirements: Mandatory local Bhutanese sponsor/partner (FDI policy requires local partners; NGO registration requires a sponsoring agency).
Est. cost & time: Low fees, 2-8 weeks once a local sponsor is secured
Notes: No direct foreign formation - a Bhutanese sponsor or partner organization is required. Small, tightly controlled NGO ecosystem; English used in official filings.

Main charitable entity types: NGO (NGO Law 2015, NGO Registration Committee), foundation/association under the Hezb and Foundations Act
Key local requirements: Registration through the NGO Registration Committee (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) with local offices; effective operation requires local partners and security access.
Est. cost & time: Low nominal fees, months to process; security and access risks dominate
Notes: Severe political risk: Taliban administration since 2021, sanctions on funds to Afghanistan, widespread donor suspension. Not a practical registration venue for most foreign founders.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (Public Trusts Act 1921, as amended, registered with MIRA), society, non-profit company
Key local requirements: Trust registered with MIRA (Maldives Investment and Regulatory Authority) with 3+ trustees; practical requirement of resident local trustees and a Maldivian registered office.
Notes: Most expats use the MIRA-registered public trust with local resident trustees and a local manager. English used in filings; annual returns and audited accounts required by MIRA.

Main charitable entity types: company limited by guarantee (CAC), trust (deed), NGO (NCMM-registered)
Key local requirements: CAC registration of a company limited by guarantee with local resident directors/office, then registration with the NCMM (Nigerian Committee on Foreign Non-Governmental Organizations) and a Ministry of Interior Operational Readiness Certificate if receiving foreign funds
Notes: Most structured path in West Africa but multi-layered; NCMM registration and ORC are the foreigner bottlenecks; English language; strong expat NGO sector in Lagos/Abuja

Main charitable entity types: company limited by guarantee, registered charity (Charities Commission, Act 1035 of 2020), trust
Key local requirements: Charitable purpose with objects meeting the Charities Act test; Ghana Charities Commission registration; Ghana-located principal office (directors may be foreign)
Notes: Most foreigner-friendly framework in the list: no local-national director requirement under the Companies Act 2019 (Act 992); Charities Commission registration has been operational since ~2021; English language

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée, fondation, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Associations formed by declaration at the préfecture (Law n° 2022-443 of 15 Aug 2022 on OSCs) with local office; foreign-funded NGOs also need authorization from the Ministry of the Interior
Notes: 2022 OSC law modernized the regime (declaration for associations, authorization for foreign-funded NGOs); French-only bureaucracy; Abidjan has active local law firms that handle expat NGO setups

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Declaration filed at the Direction de l'Administration Générale et des Cultes (Law n° 2015-04/PRB of 30 Jan 2016 on NGOs); local registered office; no local-national officer requirement
Notes: One of the more open, stable regimes in francophone West Africa; French-only; Cotonou has NGOs/lawyers familiar with expat filings

Main charitable entity types: association, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Declaration/authorization of an association under Law n° 2000-17 of 11 Aug 2000 on NGOs; local registered office; French-language documents
Notes: Administrative practice varies by préfecture; some steps in practice require in-person filing at the Mairie or prefecture in Lomé; French-only

Main charitable entity types: association (authorized), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Prior government authorization under Law n° 014/1997-AN on associations; a 2018 constitutional amendment bars NGOs that receive foreign funding above a threshold from operating
Notes: High political risk: 2018 constitutional ban on foreign-funded NGOs, 2022–2025 military rule, repeated suspensions of international NGOs (e.g. 2023–24 expulsions); effectively impractical for a foreign-funded charity

Main charitable entity types: association (loi 01-019 du 20 juin 2001), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Association registration with the Direction de l'Administration Générale (Law n° 2001-019); local office; French-language filings; authorization regime for foreign-funded NGOs in practice
Notes: Political instability (2020–2024 coups, ongoing conflict); security situation in many regions makes on-ground operations difficult; Bamako filings are French-only

Main charitable entity types: association (loi L/2010/004 du 3 janv 2010), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Declaration of an association under Law L/2010/004; local registered office in Conakry; French-language documents
Notes: 2010 association law uses a declaration regime (more open than the old authorization system); French-only; military rule since 2021 adds some political risk but NGO sector remains active

Main charitable entity types: associação, organização não governamental (ONG)
Key local requirements: Registration of an association under Lei n.º 5/VI/96 de 21 de Dezembro de 1996 (regime de registo); local office; Portuguese-language filings
Notes: Repeated military coups (7 since independence), fragile state capacity, weak enforcement of registrations; Portuguese (not French) documents; practical operations very difficult

Main charitable entity types: association déclarée (décret-loi de 1965, modèle 1901), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Simple declaration of an association at the Direction de l'Action Sociale (1965 decree, French 1901 model); local registered office; French-language documents
Notes: Stable, well-established association culture; declaration regime is the easiest in francophone West Africa; 2022/2023 framework on foreign-funded NGOs (OSC law) adds a reporting layer for foreign funders; French-only

Main charitable entity types: society (Societies Act, Cap 303), company limited by guarantee
Key local requirements: Registration of a society with the Registrar of Societies under the Societies Act 1972 (or Companies Act 1964 for a CLG); local office; English-language filings
Notes: English language, stable democracy; 2022 NGO Bill has been in draft years without enactment, so the old 1972 Societies Act still applies; Banjul filings manageable with a local agent

Main charitable entity types: company limited by guarantee (Companies Act 2013), trust, charitable society
Key local requirements: Registration of a non-profit company limited by guarantee with the Companies Registry; local registered office; English-language documents
Notes: English language; 2022 NGO Bill pending, so existing NGO/charitable-society registration practices continue; Freetown has expat-friendly law firms; registry throughput is slower than Ghana

Main charitable entity types: non-governmental organization (NGO Act 2015), limited liability company (non-profit), trust
Key local requirements: NGO registration under the NGO Act of 2015 (Act No. 11 of 2015) with a local principal officer, local office, and a US$150 (local) fee; three-year permit renewal cycle
Notes: English language; the 2015 Act is the operative law (it replaced the older NGO Bill regime); permits must be renewed every 3 years; local principal officer requirement is the main hurdle for a fully foreign board

Main charitable entity types: association (loi 93-010 du 28 avril 1993), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Key local requirements: Registration of an association with the Direction de l'Administration Générale under Law 93-010; local registered office; French-language filings; practical authorization hurdles for foreign-funded NGOs
Notes: Military rule since 2023; security situation in the north (Sahel conflict); Niamey filings are French-only; some discretionary elements in approvals

Main charitable entity types: state-run public organization (no independent charitable sector)
Key local requirements: no meaningful independent charity registration; foreign involvement barred in practice
Notes: No independent charitable pathway; no GfN. Excluded from any practical plan.

Main charitable entity types: public organization (NGO) / public foundation registered with Ministry of Justice
Key local requirements: Russian-language filings, foreign-agent law risks for foreign-linked orgs, sanctions on AU side
Notes: No GfN. Sanctions + foreign-agent regime make this unsuitable for an Australian founder.
